newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to try Colombians, German for cocaine haul.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to try Colombians, German for cocaine haul.

text.p: Morocco said on Friday it would put on trial four Colombians and a German for smuggling six tonnes of pure cocaine which local experts estimated was worth $1.5 billion.

"Four Colombians travelling with false Panamanean passports and a German were arrested and charged with cocaine trafficking," Interior Minister Driss Basri told a news conference in Rabat. "They will appear before Kenitra court once the investigation is finished."

Flanked by a group of drug experts, senior security officials and King Hassan's top adviser Andre Azoulay, Basri said the cocaine was accidently washed up on Morocco's Atlantic coast between June 21 and July 10.
"Morocco was not the destination neither the purchaser," he said.

Basri did not give names of the suspected traffickers neither the street value of the cocaine seized. But the authoritative La Vie Economique newspaper reported on Friday that the cocaine haul was estimated by experts to be worth $1.5 billion.

The first cocaine was discovered last month by children and fishermen on a Casablanca beach when they opened plastic bags and tasted the white powder inside which they tought was milk powder, the minister said.

"The ship named Duanas, which is seized by Moroccan security forces in Kenitra, belonged to the British Royal Navy and was bought earlier this year by private individuals in the United Kingdom for $395,000. It was registered in Belize," Basri said.
Kenitra is located on the Atlantic coast 35 km (20 miles) north of Rabat.
According to governor Moheiddine Amzazi, the ship visited Morocco's southern city of Agadir with a crew of four British nationals who left Morocco later.
It was not known whether the four were identified or not.
In June the ship sailed for a high sea zone off of the Canary Islands where the crew took on board the cocaine imported from Cartagena, north of Colombia for Spanish province of Galicia, Amzazi said.
On its way to Spain, the ship "had engine troubles" between El-jadida and Casablanca on the Atlantic coast. It called for urgent assistance which was granted by Moroccans, he said.
The drug cargo was thrown overboard before the arrival of Moroccan patrol units to rescue the ship, he added.
Two Spanish nationals who were on the ship and involved in the cocaine trafficking escaped and a police investigation was undergoing in Spain, an interior ministry official said.

Interior ministry officials on Tuesday held a meeting with experts from France, Spain, Italy, Portugal, Germany, Britain and United States to discuss the seized cocaine and its international implications, Basri said.
"Morocco briefed the experts on the cocaine which invaded its beaches...Morocco has showed its willingness to cooperate with the international community against this poison," Basri said.
He said Morocco is expecting an urgent international meeting on drug trafficking in Morocco in the future but gave no date.

Morocco has shown it was particularly concerned in the past two years over drug trafficking which has focused largely on cannabis, much of it produced in the north of the African country just across the Mediterranean from Spain.

Morocco launched a crackdown on drug smuggling last year, and the interior minister said recently it had seized 103 tonnes of cannabis and 91 kgs (200 pounds) of cocaine bound for European market in 1996.
It had also arrested more than 18,000 drug traffickers, including 342 foreigners most of them Europeans.
